description:
Tier 1, needs nothing: radix-2 iterative FFT, direct and FFT-based convolution, and polyphase resampling are loops over [f64] with sin/cos/sqrt, all in today's subset. People wrap fftw or use Nx for these; on Nerves and in audio/metrics pipelines a yielding, dependency-free kernel is attractive.

Kernels: `fft(re :: [f64], im :: [f64]) :: {[f64], [f64]}` for power-of-two n (a non-power-of-two length raises; Bluestein is a follow-up), with bit-reversal permutation and precomputed twiddles in an alloc'd array; `convolve(a, b) :: [f64]` direct for small b, via fft for large; `resample(x :: [f64], up :: i64, down :: i64) :: [f64]` with a windowed-sinc filter built in the kernel.

Elixir baselines: pure Elixir with tuples or :array for the butterfly loop (first pass, then optimise); Nx.fft on the binary backend and on EXLA reported beside (the Nx-boundary research, docs/research/nx-boundary.md, says where Nx is the right answer: large batched transforms).

Bit-exactness: the twiddle factors must be computed the same way in both modes (:math.cos/sin in Elixir mode, cos/sin from libm natively) and libm's cos is not guaranteed identical to the BEAM's... it is the same libm on the same machine, so agreement should hold; if it does not, document it as the first float limit of this kind and compare with a tolerance in the example (not in the agreement property).

Realistic size: n = 1024 to 1M points; measure 4096 (audio frame) and 1M.

Expected verdict: good vs pure Elixir; marginal vs Nx binary backend; poor vs EXLA for large n.

Done when: agreement holds (or the libm limit is documented), verdicts measured, README row added.
title: FFT, convolution and resampling over [f64] vs Nx and pure Elixir
